title: Framework Selection and Architecture
keywords: avoiding framework-specific assumptions in language fundamentals
subtopics: Avoiding framework-specific assumptions in language fundamentals.
learning_outcomes: Explain what framework selection and architecture contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: project complexity.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. In this lesson, focus on project complexity; then compare it with ecosystem support. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use framework selection and architecture when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Frameworks provide conventions and reusable components for routing, dependency management, validation, persistence, and queues. Learn the underlying HTTP/security concepts first and verify the selected framework's supported versions. For framework selection and architecture, begin with project complexity. Also distinguish ecosystem support; learning and maintenance cost; security and update cadence. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
